feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Here's what happened on day 2 of the UN General Assembly
entry.summary: Iran and Ukraine take center stage at the UN as diplomats push to contain two wars threatening global stability.

entry.title: Does the UN have a future?
entry.summary: NPR's Mary Louise Kelly speaks with former U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Susan Rice about the relevance of the United Nations in 2026.

entry.title: Seth MacFarlane sings the Muppets
entry.summary: Seth MacFarlane is best known for creating Family Guy and American Dad! He's also an accomplished singer. Now, he's out with a new record of Muppets songs.

entry.title: As Xi meets Trump tomorrow, how do people in China view the U.S. now?
entry.summary: As Xi Jinping heads to the White House, polls show Americans feeling their best days are behind them. But what does America look like from China?

entry.title: Judge appears skeptical of White House ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico
entry.summary: We get the latest in the court battle between major news outlets and the Trump administration that revoked their access to the White House.

entry.title: Understanding Jensen Huang's AI optimism and how it influences President Trump
entry.summary: The Nvidia CEO is a relentless AI optimist with the president's ear. Stephen Witt, author of The Thinking Machine, tells NPR's Juana Summers how their relationship could shape the future of AI.

entry.title: How to understand Trump's national security defense in his press ban
entry.summary: NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with Andrew Weissmann, a legal analyst and former federal prosecutor, about the Trump administration's rationale for banning three news outlets from the White House.

entry.title: What painter Sliman Mansour told NPR about Palestinian rights and art before he died
entry.summary: Born a year before Israel's creation, Palestinian artist Sliman Mansour spent his life painting the faces and landscapes of Israeli occupation. He died in August aged 79, and was buried in the occupied West Bank.

entry.title: Results are in from the newest NPR/PBS News/Marist poll
entry.summary: People say they are more likely to choose a Democrat to represent them in Congress, and feel Democrats would be better at tackling top issues like the economy and foreign policy.

entry.title: FBI records point to possible congressional pay-for-play scheme
entry.summary: NPR's Juana Summers talks with Avi Asher-Schapiro of ProPublica about the connections between a defense contractor and Sen. Susan Collins of Maine, and how the FBI was, at one time, looking into it.
